analysis: The supplied units are head-side excerpts of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json (lines 6862-9135). They are golden test vectors for the prompt contract: request_body, provider_body, template_input, plan (token counts and chain hashes) and token_ids. I found no executable code, authorization logic, key handling, network surface or secret material. The patch metadata shows only vector regeneration: an added additional_context.enable_thinking=false field in template_input, changed prompt_token_count values, changed chain hashes and shortened token_id lists. The visible excerpts show nothing that weakens the TB-002, TB-007, TB-011 or T-041 controls. Examined cases: tool_call_arguments_bridge, tool_function_extra_keys and tools. Their template_input lines (e.g. 8640-8642) carry additional_context.enable_thinking=false. The tool_choice case injects forced-call instructions into the system and user messages (8611-8615). Those messages are client-controlled and derived from the declared tool name, so no privilege boundary is crossed. Prefix-cache chain hashes bind to prompt_contract_id, so cache keys remain scoped to the contract. Remaining integration questions I could not verify from this batch: whether the Swift and Go implementations that consume these vectors produce identical contract IDs and chain hashes, and whether the cache scope_id and prompt_contract_id derivation, which affects T-041 cross-tenant cache sharing, changed in unseen code. The base text and the other hunks (lines ~3020-4003 and ~43739-54088) were not supplied as units. The excerpt boundary of this batch also ends mid-case at line 9135 (the unicode vector).
